patterns.comment: Compile-time data. A record with ** in positions 1-3 introduces the file translation table, the alternate collating sequence, or an array or table loaded at compile time. Everything after it is data, so the end pattern is a sentinel that never matches and the block runs to the end of the source. The (?!free) guard keeps the RPG IV **FREE line out of this rule.
patterns.name: variable.other.rpg.ctarrays

patterns.comment: The ** marker itself, so the introducer reads differently from the data that follows it.
patterns.name: string.other.rpg.ctarray

patterns.comment: Trailing comment area. F, L, I and O specifications reserve positions 75-80, E reserves 58-80, and C reserves 60-80. Positions 1-5 are matched with . rather than \s so that a line carrying a page and line number keeps its comment.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpg

patterns.comment: Comment statement: an asterisk in position 7. Position 6 may hold the specification letter, so I* and C* are comments too.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpg

patterns.comment: Positions 1-2 page number and 3-5 line number. The compiler ignores both, so they are dimmed rather than highlighted. This runs before the constant and keyword rules so that a numeric sequence number is claimed here rather than being scoped as a numeric literal, and after the comment and compile-time data rules, which own the whole line including these positions.
patterns.name: comment.gutter

patterns.comment: Control specification position 19, date format: M month/day/year, D day/month/year, Y year/month/day.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.h.datefmt

patterns.comment: Control specification position 20, date edit. Any character may be the date separator, and & means a blank separator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.h.datedit

patterns.comment: Control specification position 18, currency symbol. Any character except 0 * , . & - C or R.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.h.currency

patterns.comment: Position 21, decimal notation. The entry sets the character that separates whole numbers from decimal fractions and the one that groups thousands, and it also sets the notation for the user date. Blank takes a period for the decimal and a comma for the separator; I and J swap them; D keeps the period with a day/month/year user date. Edit words are unaffected. RPG II called this entry inverted print, which is worth knowing when reading older listings.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.h.decnotation

patterns.comment: Control specification position 26, alternate collating sequence. S is the only entry; blank means the normal sequence.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.h.altseq

patterns.comment: Control specification position 43, file translation. F means a file translation table follows the source.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.h.filetrans

patterns.comment: Position 15, debug. A 1 makes the DEBUG and DUMP operations active and places the compiler-generated symbols in the symbol table. Blank is the alternative, so the entry is a closed set of one.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.h.debug

patterns.comment: Position 41, forms alignment. A 1 lets the first line print repeatedly so the operator can line up the printer forms. Blank is the alternative, so the entry is a closed set of one.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.h.formsalign

patterns.comment: Position 57, transparency check. A 1 makes the compiler scan literals and constants for DBCS characters. Hexadecimal literals are not checked. Blank is the alternative, so the entry is a closed set of one.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.h.transparency

patterns.comment: File description position 15, file type: I input, O output, U update, C combined.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.type

patterns.comment: File description position 16, file designation: P primary, S secondary, R record address, T array or table, F full procedural.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.designation

patterns.comment: File description position 17, end of file. E means all records must be processed before the program ends.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.eof

patterns.comment: File description position 18, sequence of match fields: A ascending, D descending.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.sequence

patterns.comment: File description position 19, file format: F program described, E externally described. The rules below key off this position to tell the two layouts apart.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.format

patterns.comment: File description positions 24-27, record length of a program described file, right adjusted. The lookahead keeps the rule off an entry that is entirely blank.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.recordlen

patterns.comment: File description position 28, limits processing. L means sequential within limits by a record address file.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.mode

patterns.comment: File description positions 29-30, length of the key field or record address, right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.keyfieldlen

patterns.comment: File description position 31, record address type of a program described file: A character keys, P packed keys.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.addrtype

patterns.comment: File description position 32, file organization: I indexed, T record address file holding record numbers.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.organization

patterns.comment: File description positions 33-34, overflow indicator. OA through OG and OV.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.ovind

patterns.comment: File description position 39, extension code: E an extension specification follows, L a line counter specification follows.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.extncode

patterns.comment: File description positions 40-46, device name.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.device

patterns.comment: File description position 53, continuation line. K means positions 54-67 carry a continuation option. Unlike the entries above, this is not anchored to the file format letter in position 19, because a separate continuation line leaves positions 7-18 blank and may carry an external record format name in 19-28. A K here marks a continuation line whether it sits on the main line or on one of its own.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.continuation

patterns.comment: File description position 66, file addition. A allows records to be added to the file.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.addition

patterns.comment: File description positions 71-72, file condition. U1 through U8 name an external indicator, UC conditions the file on any of them.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.f.condition

patterns.comment: File description position 31 of an externally described file, record address type. K means the file is processed by key.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.fx.addrtype

patterns.comment: File description positions 54-59 of a continuation line, the option name, anchored to the K in position 53. There is no word boundary after the name: the field is six wide, so RENAME and PRTCTL fill it exactly and the argument in position 60 begins immediately. Shorter names are padded with blanks, so no boundary is needed. IND is listed before ID so the longer name is tried first.
patterns.name: support.function.rpg.f.option

patterns.comment: Extension positions 33-35, entries per record of a compile-time or prerun-time array, right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.entriesrecord

patterns.comment: Extension positions 36-39, number of entries in the array or table, right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.entriestable

patterns.comment: Extension positions 40-42, length of each entry, right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.entrylen

patterns.comment: Extension position 43, data format of the array or table: P packed, B binary, L or R signed.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.pblr

patterns.comment: Extension position 44, decimal positions.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.dec

patterns.comment: Extension position 45, sequence: A ascending, D descending.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.seq

patterns.comment: Extension positions 52-54, entry length of the alternating array or table, right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.len

patterns.comment: Extension position 55, data format of the alternating array or table.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.altpblr

patterns.comment: Extension position 56, decimal positions of the alternating array or table.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.altdec

patterns.comment: Extension position 57, sequence of the alternating array or table.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.e.altseq

patterns.comment: Line counter positions 15-17, lines per page, 2 through 112. The entry ends in position 17 and leading zeros may be omitted, so a two digit value is right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.l.lineno

patterns.comment: Line counter positions 18-19, FL, marking the preceding entry as the form length.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.l.formlen

patterns.comment: Line counter positions 20-22, overflow line number, right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.l.ovlineno

patterns.comment: Line counter positions 23-24, OL, marking the preceding entry as the overflow line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.l.ovline

patterns.comment: Input positions 19-20 of a data structure statement, DS.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.ds

patterns.comment: Input position 17 of a data structure statement. E means the subfields are described externally.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.ds.number

patterns.comment: Input position 18 of a data structure statement: I initialize the whole structure, S program status data structure, U data area data structure.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.ds.option

patterns.comment: Input position 43 of a named constant statement, C, marking positions 21-42 as the constant and 53-58 as its name.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.constant

patterns.comment: Input position 8 of a data structure subfield. I initializes the subfield to the value in positions 21-42.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.subfinit

patterns.comment: Input positions 14-16, logical relationship. AND continues the record identification codes of the line above, OR starts an alternative record type. Positions 7-13 must be blank on such a line, which is what this anchors to. Listed before the sequence entry because AND occupies positions 15 and 16 as well, and those would otherwise be read as a sequence.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.logical

patterns.comment: Input positions 15-16, sequence. Two alphabetic characters mean no sequence checking; two digits request it.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.seq

patterns.comment: Input position 17, number: 1 if only one record of this type may appear, N if more than one may.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.num

patterns.comment: Input position 18, option. O means the record type is optional.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.option

patterns.comment: Input positions 19-20, record identifying indicator: 01-99, H1-H9, L1-L9, LR, U1-U8 or RT. ** marks a look-ahead record.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.recordid

patterns.comment: Input positions 21-27, first record identification code: position, optional N, C character or Z zone or D digit, and the character to compare. The identifying character may itself be a blank, which is stripped when source is stored as a text file, so the last position matches either a character or the end of the line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.id1

patterns.comment: Input positions 28-34, second record identification code. The identifying character may itself be a blank, which is stripped when source is stored as a text file, so the last position matches either a character or the end of the line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.id2

patterns.comment: Input positions 35-41, third record identification code. The identifying character may itself be a blank, which is stripped when source is stored as a text file, so the last position matches either a character or the end of the line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.id3

patterns.comment: Input position 43, internal data format of the field: P packed, B binary, L or R signed.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.pblr

patterns.comment: Input positions 44-47, starting position of the field in the record, right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.from

patterns.comment: Input positions 48-51, end position of the field in the record, right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.to

patterns.comment: Input position 52, decimal positions of a numeric field.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.decpos

patterns.comment: Input positions 59-60, control level: L1 through L9.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.ctrl

patterns.comment: Input positions 61-62, matching fields: M1 through M9.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.matching

patterns.comment: Input positions 63-64, field record relation: 01-99, H1-H9, L1-L9, MR, RT or U1-U8.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.fldrcdrel

patterns.comment: Input positions 65-66, field indicator set on when the numeric field is greater than zero: 01-99, H1-H9, U1-U8 or RT.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.posfld

patterns.comment: Input positions 67-68, field indicator set on when the numeric field is less than zero.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.negfield

patterns.comment: Input positions 69-70, field indicator set on when the field is zero or blank.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.i.zeroblank

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 7-8, control level: L0 total time, L1-L9 control break, LR last record, SR subroutine, AN and OR continuation of the conditioning indicators. L0 uses a zero.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.level

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 9-11, first conditioning indicator. A blank in position 9 tests for on, N tests for off.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.n01

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 12-14, second conditioning indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.n02

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 15-17, third conditioning indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.n03

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 49-51, result field length, right adjusted.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.len

patterns.comment: Calculation position 52, decimal positions of the result field.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.decpos

patterns.comment: Calculation position 53, operation extender: H half adjust, N read without lock, P pad the result with blanks.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.opext

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 54-55, high resulting indicator: 01-99, KA-KN, KP-KY, H1-H9, L1-L9, LR, OA-OG, OV, U1-U8 or RT.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.hi

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 56-57, low resulting indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.lo

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 58-59, equal resulting indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.c.eq

patterns.comment: Output positions 14-16, logical relationship, relating the conditioning indicators of this line to the line above. Positions 7-13 must be blank on such a line.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.logical

patterns.comment: Output position 15, record type: H heading, D detail, T total, E exception.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.type

patterns.comment: Output positions 16-18, record addition: ADD writes a new record, DEL deletes one.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.adddel

patterns.comment: Output position 16, fetch overflow or release. F fetches overflow on a printer file, R releases a workstation device after output. Neither collides with the ADD and DEL of the entry above, which occupy the same position.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.fetch

patterns.comment: Output positions 23-25, first output indicator. N in position 23 tests for off. 1P conditions a line on the first page.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.n01

patterns.comment: Output positions 26-28, second output indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.n02

patterns.comment: Output positions 29-31, third output indicator.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.n03

patterns.comment: Output position 38, edit code: 1-4 and A-D, J-Q are the combination codes, 5-9 are user defined, X, Y and Z are the simple codes. Zero is not an edit code.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.editcode

patterns.comment: Output position 39, blank after. B resets the field once it has been written.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.blankafter

patterns.comment: Output positions 40-43, end position. The entry ends in position 43 and is one of nnnn, +nnn or -nnn for a displacement from the previous field, or K1-K8 for the length of a program described WORKSTN format name.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.endpos

patterns.comment: Output position 44, data format: P packed, B binary, L or R signed. Blank writes the field zoned or as character data.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.o.pblr

patterns.comment: Indicators referred to as data: *IN the array, *IN,xx an element of it, and *INxx the one-position field for indicator xx.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.indicator

patterns.comment: Numeric constant in positions 21-42 of an input specification, with an optional leading sign, an optional decimal point, and the optional trailing hyphen of a continued constant.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.rpg

patterns.comment: Numeric literal: digits with an optional decimal point.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.rpg

patterns.comment: Numeric literal in calculation factor 1, position 18. A sign, if present, is the leftmost character of the literal rather than an operator. Factor 1 follows the conditioning indicators, so a literal there can begin immediately after a word character and the general rule cannot see a word boundary.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.rpg

patterns.comment: Numeric literal in calculation factor 2, position 33. A sign, if present, is the leftmost character of the literal rather than an operator. Factor 2 begins in the character after the operation field, so Z-ADD1000 offers no word boundary for the general rule to match on.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.rpg

patterns.comment: Reserved words with special functions. The list is chapter 12 of the reference plus *EXT and *NOKEY, which are special values of the DSPLY and CLEAR operations.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg

patterns.comment: Reserved words written without a leading asterisk: the user date fields and the page number fields PAGE and PAGE1 through PAGE7. The fields of a specification butt against each other, so factor 2 of Z-ADDUDATE begins in the middle of a word and a plain word boundary would miss it. Rather than drop the boundary altogether, which let a name such as NUPAGE match, the word is accepted either where a non-name character precedes it or where it begins one of the fields that can be butted against: factor 1 in 18, the output field name in 32, factor 2 in 33 and the result field in 43.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg

patterns.comment: The /TITLE compiler directive in positions 7-12. The heading text in 14-74 is prose, so it reads as a comment. Anchored with a lookbehind rather than ^ so that the rule still matches once the gutter rule has consumed positions 1-5.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg.precompiler.title

patterns.comment: The heading text that /TITLE prints on the compiler listing.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpg.precompiler.title

patterns.comment: The /COPY compiler directive in positions 7-11, followed in 13-44 by the member to merge in, written library/file,member or file.library,member in the System/38 environment.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg.precompiler.copy

patterns.comment: The name of the member being copied.
patterns.name: string.other.rpg.precompiler.copy

patterns.comment: Anything after the member name is ignored by the compiler.
patterns.name: comment.other.rpg.precompiler.copy

patterns.comment: The /SPACE compiler directive in positions 7-12, with the number of lines to space in 14-16, left adjusted. Its operand is scoped separately, the way /TITLE scopes its heading text and /COPY its member name.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg.precompiler

patterns.comment: The number of lines to space on the compiler listing, 1 through 112.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.rpg

patterns.comment: The remaining compiler directives, /EJECT and /SPACE, in positions 7-12. TITLE and COPY are listed too because this rule also catches them when the rules above do not. Position 6 is blank or repeats the preceding specification letter.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg.precompiler

patterns.comment: Position 6, the specification letter that says which form the line is: H control, F file description, E extension, L line counter, I input, C calculation, O output.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 28-32, the structured and compare operations that take a comparison suffix. The suffix is GT, LT, EQ, NE, GE or LE. Listed before the plain operation codes so that IFEQ is one token rather than IF followed by EQ.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg

patterns.comment: Separators and arithmetic signs: the colon between the parts of a compound factor, the comma, and the plus, minus and period of a numeric literal or edit word.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg

patterns.comment: Calculation positions 28-32, the operation code. Anchored to the operation field so that a field or file name spelled like an operation is left alone.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg

patterns.comment: Hexadecimal constant in positions 21-42 of an input specification. Ends at the closing quote or at position 43, whichever comes first, so a continued constant does not swallow the C in position 43 and the name in 53-58.
patterns.name: string.other.rpg.hex

patterns.comment: Character constant in positions 21-42 of an input specification. Ends at the closing quote or at position 43, whichever comes first, for the same reason as the rule above.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.rpg

patterns.comment: Hexadecimal literal, X'xx'. Written before the quoted literal rule so the leading X is part of the literal. The end pattern includes a newline so that an unterminated literal, such as the first line of a continued named constant, stops at the end of its line instead of running on into the next one.
patterns.name: string.other.rpg.hex

patterns.comment: Character literal. RPG has no escape character; a quote inside a literal is written twice, which ends this match and starts another.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.rpg

patterns.comment: An embedded SQL statement. EXEC SQL occupies positions 8-16 with a slash in position 7 and a C in position 6; the statement runs from 17 to 74 and continues on lines carrying a plus in position 7.
patterns.name: variable.other.rpg.sql

patterns.comment: The /EXEC SQL that opens the statement.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg.sql.precompiler

patterns.comment: The C in position 6 that every line of the statement carries, together with the plus in position 7 that marks a continuation line.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg.sql.c

patterns.comment: The /END-EXEC that closes an embedded SQL statement, in positions 7-16.
patterns.name: keyword.other.rpg.sql.precompiler

patterns.comment: Fields of the SQL communication area, recognised anywhere in the program because they are tested in ordinary calculations after each statement. The precompiler inserts the SQLCA into the input specifications itself, so these are program fields rather than reserved words, but the language defines them rather than the programmer. RPG/400 names are limited to six characters, which is why IBM truncates the standard SQLCA names. Neither end carries a word boundary: factor 2 begins in the character after the operation field, and a six character name fills the result field exactly, so a length in positions 49-51 would butt against it. The longer RPG IV spellings are listed before the truncated ones so SQLCODE is not matched as SQLCOD followed by E.
patterns.name: variable.language.rpg.sql

patterns.comment: SQL line comment. RPG/400 allows one wherever a blank is allowed, except between the keywords EXEC and SQL.
patterns.name: comment.line.rpg.sql

patterns.comment: SQL global variables.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.sql.globals

patterns.comment: A name followed by an opening parenthesis, which is how a function call is written.
patterns.name: support.function.rpg.sql

patterns.comment: A qualified name, written schema.object or schema/object.
patterns.name: constant.language.rpg.sql.schema

patterns.comment: A host variable, written with a leading colon.
patterns.name: variable.parameter.rpg.sql

patterns.comment: Hexadecimal literal in an SQL statement, X'xx'.
patterns.name: string.other.rpg.sql.hex

patterns.comment: Character literal in an SQL statement. A quote inside a literal is written twice, which closes this match and opens another, the same way the RPG character literal behaves.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.rpg.sql

patterns.comment: DB2 for i reserved words. This is the same list the RPGLE grammar carries, kept identical so the two do not drift, plus the WHENEVER conditions SQLERROR, SQLWARNING and FOUND, which only ever appear in embedded SQL. The list is sorted in reverse so that a longer word is tried before a shorter one it begins with.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.rpg.sql.reserved

patterns.comment: Numeric literal in an SQL statement. The leading word boundary keeps the rule off the digits of an identifier such as CUST1. A sign in front of a literal is scoped by the operator rule below, as it is elsewhere in the grammar. This sits after the comment and literal rules so digits inside those are not picked out.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.rpg.sql

patterns.comment: SQL operators: comparison, arithmetic and concatenation. Longer operators are listed first so that >= is one token rather than > followed by =. The comment rule above runs first, so the -- that opens a comment is never seen as two minus signs, and the qualified name rule runs first, so the slash in schema/object is not division. The RPGLE grammar shares this file's reserved word list but has no operator rule yet.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.rpg.sql
